blocks.text: SUBJECT 12 – MICROPROCESSORS AND ITS APPLICATIONS (SUCA202)
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: UNIT I – MICROPROCESSOR INTRODUCTION
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 2-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 1. Define a microprocessor.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: A microprocessor is a programmable, clock-driven, register-based electronic device that reads binary instructions, processes data and controls operations according to the program.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 2. Name the three main parts of a microcomputer system.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: Microprocessor, memory and input/output devices/interfaces.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 3. What is assembly language?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: Assembly language is a symbolic low-level language that uses mnemonics to represent machine instructions.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 4. What is an assembler?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: An assembler translates assembly-language instructions into machine-code instructions.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: UNIT II – 8085 ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 2-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 1. What is the word length of 8085?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: 8 bits.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 2. How many address lines does 8085 have?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: 16 address lines.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 3. What is the maximum address space of 8085?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: 2^16=65,536 byte locations, or 64 KB.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 4. What is the function of the Program Counter?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: The Program Counter holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched/executed.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 5. What is the function of the Stack Pointer?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: The Stack Pointer holds the memory address of the top of the stack.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 6. Name the five condition flags in 8085.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: Sign (S), Zero (Z), Auxiliary Carry (AC), Parity (P) and Carry (CY).
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 7. What is ALE?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: Address Latch Enable is used to latch the lower address byte from the multiplexed AD7–AD0 lines during the first part of a machine cycle.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 5-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 1. Explain the 8085 bus structure.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: The address bus carries the address of a memory location or I/O device; it is generally unidirectional from the processor. The data bus carries instructions/data and is bidirectional. The control bus carries signals that coordinate operations such as read and write. In 8085, AD7–AD0 are multiplexed address/data lines and A15–A8 carry the high-order address.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 2. Explain the 8085 register set.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: The accumulator is used by many arithmetic and logic instructions. B,C,D,E,H,L are general-purpose registers and can form BC, DE and HL pairs for selected operations. PC stores the next instruction address; SP points to the stack; the flag register records status conditions. Explain the exact register uses and diagrams from the official architecture lesson.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 3. Explain 8085 addressing modes.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: Immediate mode places data in the instruction; register mode uses a register operand; direct mode specifies the memory address; register-indirect mode uses a register pair to hold the memory address; implied mode does not explicitly state the operand because it is understood from the instruction. Give the examples in the SUCA202 instruction table.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 10-MARK QUESTION
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Draw and explain the 8085 architecture.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: Draw the architecture with ALU, accumulator, temporary register, general-purpose registers, flag register, instruction register/decoder, timing and control unit, program counter, stack pointer, address/data buffers and buses. Explain how the processor fetches an instruction, decodes it, obtains operands, executes the operation and stores the result. Add the 8-bit data bus, 16-bit address bus and 64 KB address capacity.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: UNIT III – INSTRUCTION SET AND ASSEMBLY LANGUAGE PROGRAMMING
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 2-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 1. What is an instruction set?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: The instruction set is the collection of machine instructions recognised by the processor.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 2. What does MOV A,B do?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: It copies the contents of register B into accumulator A; the source register is not changed.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 3. What does MVI A,32H do?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: It loads the immediate hexadecimal data 32H into accumulator A.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 4. What is a branch instruction?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: A branch instruction changes the normal sequence of execution by transferring control to another address, conditionally or unconditionally.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 5-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 1. Classify the 8085 instruction set.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: The main groups are data transfer, arithmetic, logical, branching/control transfer and machine/control instructions. Give examples from each group such as MOV, ADD, ANA, JMP and HLT. Use the official table for byte length, operand format and flag effects.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 2. Explain looping and counting in an 8085 program.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: Load a counter; perform the required operation; decrement or increment the counter; test whether the required number of iterations has completed; and branch to the loop start if more work remains. Explain the branch condition and show which register stores the counter.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 10-MARK QUESTION
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Explain the 8085 addressing modes and important instruction groups.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: Define immediate, register, direct, register-indirect and implied addressing. Then explain data transfer, arithmetic, logical, branch and machine-control instructions with mnemonics and sample operations. Include instruction-byte length and flag effects only when verified from the official instruction table.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: UNIT IV – ARITHMETIC, COUNTERS, TIME DELAYS, STACKS AND SUBROUTINES
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 2-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 1. What does PUSH do?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: PUSH stores a register pair on the stack.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 2. What does POP do?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: POP retrieves a value from the stack into a register pair.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 3. What does CALL do?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: CALL transfers control to a subroutine and saves the return address on the stack.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 4. What is a modulo-10 counter?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: It is a counter that cycles through ten states, typically 0 to 9, and then returns to the initial state.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 5. What is BCD?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: BCD represents each decimal digit using four bits.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 5-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 1. Explain multi-byte addition in 8085.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: Add the least significant bytes first; preserve the carry; add the next byte including the incoming carry; continue through the higher-order bytes; and store any final carry as required. Use a memory/register layout and show the carry propagation.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 2. Explain software time delay.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: A delay loop consumes processor cycles. The total delay depends on clock frequency, machine cycles per instruction and loop count. Calculate the time using the instruction timings in the official textbook. State the counter initialisation and loop branch clearly.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 3. Explain subroutine operation.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: CALL saves the return address and transfers execution to the subroutine. The subroutine performs a task and RET returns to the saved address. The stack pointer changes during call/return. Conditional call/return executes only when the specified flag condition is satisfied.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 10-MARK QUESTION
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Write the steps to design a counter or time-delay routine.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: Define the required count sequence or delay; select a register/memory counter; initialise it; write the operation performed per count; update the counter; compare/test terminal condition; branch as required; and ensure the routine terminates or repeats correctly. For a delay calculation, determine cycles per loop from the 8085 timing table, multiply by loop count and convert cycles to time using the clock period. Use exact timing data from SUCA202.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: UNIT V – BCD CONVERSION, INTERRUPTS, DMA AND MEMORY/I/O
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 2-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 1. Name the 8085 hardware interrupts.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: TRAP, RST 7.5, RST 6.5, RST 5.5 and INTR.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 2. Which 8085 interrupt is non-maskable and highest priority?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: TRAP.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 3. What is DMA?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: Direct Memory Access allows data transfer between an I/O device and memory with reduced direct CPU involvement.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 4. Distinguish RAM and ROM.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: RAM is read/write memory and is generally volatile; ROM is non-volatile memory used to retain data/instructions.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 5. What is memory-mapped I/O?
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: Memory-mapped I/O assigns I/O device registers addresses in the memory address space and accesses them using memory instructions.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 5-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 1. Explain the interrupt sequence.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: An interrupt request is recognised according to enable/mask and priority rules; the processor completes the current instruction; it acknowledges the interrupt; saves the return address/state as required; transfers control to the interrupt service routine; services the event; and returns using the appropriate return instruction. Use the 8085-specific sequence in the textbook.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 2. Compare direct I/O and memory-mapped I/O.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: Direct/isolated I/O uses a separate I/O address space and I/O-specific instructions/control signals. Memory-mapped I/O places device registers in the memory address space and uses normal memory instructions. Compare address decoding, instruction use and control signals as described in the textbook.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 3. Explain BCD and seven-segment code conversion.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: BCD encodes each decimal digit in four bits. A seven-segment display lights selected segments a–g to represent a digit. Conversion routines translate between the input code and the segment pattern; the exact pattern depends on common-anode/common-cathode connection and the coding convention. Reproduce the code table from the official book.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 10-MARK QUESTION
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Explain 8085 interrupts, DMA and memory interfacing.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: Answer: Define interrupt and describe TRAP, RST 7.5, RST 6.5, RST 5.5 and INTR. Compare priority, maskability and vectoring using the official table. Define DMA and explain bus request/control/transfer. Describe RAM/ROM interfacing and compare direct I/O with memory-mapped I/O. Use labelled diagrams and exact signal names from the textbook.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 8085 ASSEMBLY PRACTICE – BASIC ALGORITHMS
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: 1. Add two 8-bit numbers: Load the first value in A; add the second operand; store the result; account for the carry flag if the sum exceeds 8 bits. Use the memory/register addresses specified in the practical question. 2. Subtract two 8-bit numbers: Load the minuend in A; execute SUB with the subtrahend; store the result; inspect carry as borrow indication according to 8085 subtraction convention. 3. Count N data items: Initialise a counter; read/process one item; decrement counter; use a conditional jump to repeat until zero. 4. Find the largest item in a list: Load the first element as current maximum; compare each subsequent element; replace maximum when a larger element is found; continue until the list is exhausted; store the maximum. 5. Convert a decimal digit/BCD value: Identify whether the input is packed or unpacked BCD; apply the conversion sequence and table specified in the official lesson; store the result in the stated format. Do not mix BCD with pure binary representation.
blocks.subject: Microprocessors and its Applications

blocks.text: SUBJECT 13 – NUMERICAL AND STATISTICAL METHODS (SUCA203)
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: UNIT I – ERRORS, ROOTS AND SIMULTANEOUS LINEAR EQUATIONS
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 2-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 1. Define absolute error.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Absolute error is |true value−approximate value|.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 2. Define relative error.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Relative error is absolute error divided by the magnitude of the true value, when the true value is non-zero.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 3. State the bisection formula.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: c=(a+b)/2, where [a,b] is an interval with a sign change in a continuous function.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 4. State the Regula Falsi formula.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: c=[a f(b)−b f(a)]/[f(b)−f(a)].
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 5. State Newton-Raphson iteration.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: x_(n+1)=x_n−f(x_n)/f'(x_n).
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 6. What is LU decomposition?
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: LU decomposition expresses a matrix as the product of a lower triangular matrix L and an upper triangular matrix U.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 5-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 1. Compare bisection and false-position methods.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Both bracket a root using endpoints with opposite signs. Bisection uses the midpoint and halves the interval each iteration. False position uses a straight-line interpolation between endpoint function values. Bisection has predictable interval reduction; false position may converge faster in some cases but can stagnate.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 2. Explain Gauss elimination.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Form the augmented matrix; use elementary row operations to eliminate entries below the leading diagonal; obtain upper triangular form; and solve by back substitution. If a pivot is zero or unsuitable, use row pivoting as required.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 3. Explain Gauss-Seidel iteration.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Start with an initial approximation; solve each equation for one variable; update variables sequentially using the newest available values; repeat until successive approximations differ by less than the tolerance. Convergence depends on the system; diagonal dominance is a useful sufficient condition in common cases.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 10-MARK SOLVED EXAMPLE – BISECTION
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Find a root of f(x)=x²−2 in [1,2] using bisection for three iterations.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: f(1)=−1 and f(2)=2, so a root is bracketed. Iteration 1: c1=1.5; f(c1)=0.25, so retain [1,1.5]. Iteration 2: c2=1.25; f(c2)=−0.4375, so retain [1.25,1.5]. Iteration 3: c3=1.375; f(c3)=−0.109375, so retain [1.375,1.5]. The root is further approximated by repeating; the actual root is √2≈1.4142. The bracket after three iterations contains the root.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: UNIT II – NUMERICAL DIFFERENTIATION, INTEGRATION AND ODEs
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 2-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 1. State the trapezoidal rule.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: I≈h/2[y0+yn+2Σ(interior yi)].
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 2. State Simpson's 1/3 rule.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: I≈h/3[y0+yn+4Σ(odd-index interior yi)+2Σ(even-index interior yi)], with an even number of subintervals.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 3. State Simpson's 3/8 rule.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: I≈3h/8[y0+yn+3Σ(interior ordinates not at multiples of 3)+2Σ(interior ordinates at multiples of 3)], with the number of subintervals a multiple of 3.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 4. State Euler's method.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: y_(n+1)=y_n+h f(x_n,y_n) for y'=f(x,y).
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 5. What is Runge-Kutta fourth order method?
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: It is a numerical method that combines four slope estimates per step to produce a fourth-order accurate update for an initial-value ODE.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 5-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 1. Compare trapezoidal and Simpson's rules.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Trapezoidal rule approximates the curve by straight-line segments and can use any number of subintervals. Simpson's 1/3 rule fits parabolas over pairs of subintervals and requires an even number; Simpson's 3/8 rule uses cubic interpolation over groups of three subintervals and requires the number of subintervals to be a multiple of three. State the coefficient patterns.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 2. Explain Euler's and RK4 methods.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Euler's method uses the slope at the beginning of the interval: y_(n+1)=y_n+h f(x_n,y_n). RK4 computes four slopes k1,k2,k3,k4 at the beginning, two midpoint estimates and the end; it combines them with weights 1,2,2,1 divided by 6. RK4 is generally more accurate for a comparable step size on smooth problems.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 10-MARK SOLVED EXAMPLE – TRAPEZOIDAL RULE
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Approximate ∫0^2 x² dx using h=1.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: x values are 0,1,2 and y values are 0,1,4. Trapezoidal approximation = h/2[y0+y2+2y1] = 1/2[0+4+2]=3. The exact integral is 8/3≈2.6667, so the numerical error is approximately 0.3333. Show the ordinates table and formula.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: UNIT III – DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 2-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 1. Define population and sample.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Population is the complete group under study; a sample is a subset selected from that population.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 2. Define cumulative frequency.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Cumulative frequency is the running total of frequencies up to a given class/value.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 3. Define arithmetic mean.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Arithmetic mean is the sum of observations divided by the number of observations.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 4. Define median.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Median is the middle value of an ordered data set, dividing observations into two equal halves.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 5. Define mode.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Mode is the value occurring with the highest frequency.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 6. Define standard deviation.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Standard deviation is the positive square root of variance and measures spread around the mean.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 5-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 1. Compare mean, median and mode.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Mean uses all observations and is sensitive to extreme values; median is the middle ordered value and is more resistant to outliers; mode is the most frequent value and can be used for categorical data. Select the measure according to distribution shape and purpose.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 2. Explain range, mean deviation, variance and standard deviation.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Range is maximum−minimum. Mean deviation is the average absolute deviation from a selected average. Variance is the average squared deviation from the mean (with population/sample divisor depending on context). Standard deviation is the square root of variance and is expressed in the original unit.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 10-MARK SOLVED EXAMPLE – MEAN AND VARIANCE
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: For data 2,4,6,8, find mean and population variance.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Mean=(2+4+6+8)/4=5. Deviations are −3,−1,1,3; squares are 9,1,1,9; sum=20. Population variance=20/4=5. Standard deviation=√5≈2.236. If sample variance is required, divide by n−1=3, giving 20/3≈6.667; read the question carefully to identify population or sample.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: UNIT IV – PROBABILITY AND DISTRIBUTIONS
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 2-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 1. State the addition law of probability.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B)−P(A∩B).
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 2. Define conditional probability.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: P(A|B)=P(A∩B)/P(B), when P(B)>0.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 3. State the binomial distribution formula.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: P(X=x)=nCx p^x(1−p)^(n−x), x=0,...,n.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 4. State the Poisson probability formula.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 5. Define mathematical expectation.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: For a discrete random variable, E(X)=ΣxP(X=x).
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 5-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 1. Explain the conditions for a binomial distribution.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: There is a fixed number of trials; trials are independent; each trial has two outcomes (success/failure); and the probability of success p is constant. If these conditions fit, the probability of x successes is nCx p^x q^(n−x), where q=1−p.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 2. Distinguish binomial and hypergeometric distributions.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Binomial models independent trials with a constant success probability, often sampling with replacement or from a large population. Hypergeometric models sampling without replacement from a finite population with a fixed number of successes; probabilities change from draw to draw.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 10-MARK SOLVED EXAMPLE – BINOMIAL
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: A fair coin is tossed 3 times. Find the probability of exactly 2 heads.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: UNIT V – CORRELATION, REGRESSION AND SIGNIFICANCE TESTS
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 2-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 1. Define correlation.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Correlation measures the direction and strength of association between two variables; it does not by itself establish causation.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 2. What is the range of Pearson's correlation coefficient?
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: −1≤r≤+1.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 3. What is regression?
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Regression estimates the relationship between variables and is used to predict one variable from another.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 4. What is a null hypothesis?
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: H0 is the statistical statement being tested, often representing no effect/no difference or a specified population parameter value.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 5. State the chi-square statistic.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: χ²=Σ(O−E)²/E, where O is observed frequency and E is expected frequency.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 5-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 1. Distinguish correlation and regression.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: Correlation measures association and is symmetric in the two variables. Regression fits an equation to estimate/predict a dependent variable from one or more independent variables; the regression of y on x differs from x on y. Neither alone proves causation.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 2. Explain the steps of a significance test.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: State H0 and H1; choose significance level α; identify the test and assumptions; calculate the test statistic; determine a critical value or p-value with suitable degrees of freedom; make a reject/do-not-reject decision; and write a conclusion in the problem context. Do not claim a non-rejected H0 is proven true.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: 10-MARK SOLVED EXAMPLE – CHI-SQUARE
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Observed frequencies are 20 and 30, with expected frequencies 25 and 25. Calculate χ².
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: Answer: χ²=(20−25)²/25+(30−25)²/25=25/25+25/25=2. State the degrees of freedom and critical value only when the full test setup provides the required categories and significance level. This calculation alone is the test statistic, not a final decision.
blocks.subject: Numerical and Statistical Methods

blocks.text: SUBJECT 14 – PROGRAMMING IN C++ USING DATA STRUCTURES LAB (SUCA204)
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: PRACTICAL QUESTION ANSWERS
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: 1. Write the algorithm for stack PUSH and POP using an array.
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: Answer: Initialise top=−1. PUSH: if top==capacity−1 report overflow; else increment top and store the new item. POP: if top==−1 report underflow; else return data[top] and decrement top. Each operation is O(1).
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: 2. Write the algorithm for stack PUSH and POP using pointers.
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: Answer: Keep a top pointer. PUSH allocates a node, stores data, links node->next to top and updates top. POP checks top!=NULL, saves its data, moves top to top->next, deletes the old node and returns the value. Free all dynamically allocated nodes.
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: 3. Explain a queue using an array.
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: Answer: Maintain front and rear indices. ENQUEUE inserts at rear after checking the full condition; DEQUEUE removes from front after checking the empty condition. The manual may use linear or circular representation; follow its update rules. In a circular queue, the next index is (index+1) mod capacity.
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: 4. Explain a queue using pointers.
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: Answer: Maintain front and rear node pointers. On insertion, create a new node and link it after rear; if the queue is empty, set both front and rear. On deletion, remove the front node and move front to front->next; if it becomes NULL, also set rear to NULL.
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: 5. Convert the infix expression A+B*C to postfix.
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: Answer: Multiplication has higher precedence than addition, so B*C is evaluated first. The postfix expression is ABC*+.
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: 6. Evaluate postfix expression 23*54*+.
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: Answer: Push 2 and 3; * gives 6. Push 5 and 4; * gives 20. + gives 26. Final result=26.
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: 7. Explain polynomial multiplication using linked lists.
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: Answer: Multiply every term of the first polynomial by every term of the second. Multiply coefficients and add exponents. Insert each product term into the result in exponent order, combining like exponents. Remove terms with zero coefficients. Check that all term pairs have been processed.
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: 8. Explain DFS and BFS with data structures.
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: Answer: DFS uses recursion or a stack to explore a path deeply before backtracking. BFS uses a queue to explore neighbours level by level. Mark a vertex visited when it is scheduled/processed to avoid revisiting. For disconnected graphs, restart traversal from an unvisited vertex if complete coverage is required.
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: 9. What are the three binary tree traversals?
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: Answer: Preorder: Root-Left-Right; Inorder: Left-Root-Right; Postorder: Left-Right-Root.
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: 10. What tests should be performed on linked-list code?
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: Answer: Test an empty list, one-node list, insertion at the beginning/end/middle, deletion of first/last/middle node, missing search key and repeated operations. Verify all previous/next links and ensure deleted memory is released.
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: MODEL PRACTICAL VIVA
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: 1. What is underflow? Answer: Attempting to remove an item from an empty stack/queue. 2. What is overflow? Answer: Attempting to insert into a full fixed-capacity structure. 3. Why do we need a visited array in graph traversal? Answer: To avoid processing a vertex repeatedly and to prevent infinite revisiting through cycles. 4. Which data structure is used in BFS? Answer: Queue. 5. Which data structure supports recursive DFS calls? Answer: The call stack. 6. What is the advantage of a doubly linked list? Answer: Traversal in both directions; the cost is extra pointer storage and more link updates.
blocks.subject: C++ Data Structures Lab

blocks.text: SUBJECT 15 – FINANCIAL ACCOUNTING (SUCA205)
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: UNIT I – ACCOUNTING FRAMEWORK AND PROCESS
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 2-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 1. State the accounting equation.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: Assets = Liabilities + Owner's Equity (Capital).
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 2. What is the double-entry system?
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: It is a system in which every transaction records both debit and credit aspects, with total debits equal to total credits.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 3. Distinguish cash and mercantile systems.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: Under cash system, transactions are recorded when cash is received or paid. Under mercantile/accrual system, income and expenses are recorded when earned/incurred or due, even if cash has not yet moved.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 4. State the rules for nominal accounts.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: Debit all expenses and losses; credit all incomes and gains.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 5. What is a contra entry?
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: A contra entry records a transaction between cash and bank in the same Cash Book, such as cash deposited into bank or cash withdrawn from bank for office use.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 5-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 1. Explain the accounting process.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: Identify economic events; measure them in monetary terms; record them in Journal/original-entry books; classify them in Ledger accounts; summarise balances in a Trial Balance and final accounts; and communicate/interprete the information to users. Explain each stage briefly.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 2. Explain the rules of debit and credit.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: Personal: debit the receiver, credit the giver. Real: debit what comes in, credit what goes out. Nominal: debit expenses/losses, credit gains/incomes. Under the accounting equation, increases in assets and expenses are debits; increases in liabilities, capital and revenue are credits. Every journal entry must balance.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 3. Explain the purpose of Trial Balance and its limitations.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: Trial Balance lists ledger balances to check arithmetic agreement and assist in preparing final accounts. Agreement does not prove that all transactions were recorded or classified correctly; errors of omission, principle, compensating errors or errors that preserve double entry may remain.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 10-MARK QUESTION
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Journalise and post business transactions.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: For each transaction identify affected accounts, classify them, apply debit/credit rules, record date, particulars, debit and credit amounts, and add narration. Then post each debit and credit to the corresponding ledger accounts. Balance accounts and extract Trial Balance balances. Explain each transaction, not only the final totals.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: UNIT II – FINAL ACCOUNTS
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 2-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 1. What is a Trading Account?
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: It is prepared to determine gross profit or gross loss from buying and selling goods.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 2. What is a Profit and Loss Account?
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: It is prepared to determine net profit or net loss after considering indirect expenses and other incomes.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 3. What is a Balance Sheet?
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: It is a statement showing assets, liabilities and capital of a business on a particular date.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 4. What is an outstanding expense?
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: An expense incurred in the current period but not yet paid.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 5. What is a prepaid expense?
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: An expense paid in advance that relates to a future accounting period.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 5-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 1. Explain the treatment of closing stock.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: Closing stock is generally valued at cost or net realisable/market value whichever is lower, according to the textbook treatment. It appears on the credit side of Trading Account and as a current asset in the Balance Sheet when given as an adjustment. If it is already in the Trial Balance, follow the prescribed treatment for that problem.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 2. Explain outstanding and prepaid expenses.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: Outstanding expense is added to the related current-period expense and shown as a liability. Prepaid expense is deducted from the current-period expense and shown as an asset. These treatments apply the matching concept.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 3. Explain bad debts and provision for doubtful debts.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: Bad debts are amounts written off when considered irrecoverable; they are charged to P&L and deducted from debtors. A provision for doubtful debts estimates possible future non-collection and is deducted from debtors. If an old provision exists, calculate only the required adjustment after writing off additional bad debts, following the textbook method.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 10-MARK WORKED CALCULATION
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Given net sales Rs.1,00,000; opening stock Rs.10,000; net purchases Rs.60,000; direct wages Rs.5,000; closing stock Rs.15,000; indirect expenses Rs.12,000; other income Rs.2,000. Find gross and net profit.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: COGS=10,000+60,000+5,000−15,000=60,000. Gross Profit=1,00,000−60,000=40,000. Net Profit=40,000+2,000−12,000=30,000. In the complete final-account question, prepare Trading A/c, P&L A/c and Balance Sheet and apply every adjustment with its required two effects.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: UNIT III – DEPARTMENTAL ACCOUNTS
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 2-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 1. What is departmental accounting?
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: It is the preparation of separate accounts for departments of one business to determine and compare their financial results.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 2. What is an interdepartmental transfer?
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: It is the transfer of goods or services from one department to another department of the same business.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 3. What is a stock reserve?
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: It is an adjustment to remove unrealised internal profit included in closing stock of goods transferred between departments at a profit.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 5-MARK QUESTION
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Explain the basis of allocation of common departmental expenses.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: Allocate each expense on a basis that reflects the benefit or usage: rent by floor area; repairs/depreciation by value or use of departmental assets; lighting/electricity by power points, wattage, units or machine hours; insurance by stock value or relevant asset value; manager's salary by time devoted. Use the basis specified in the question. Direct expenses are charged to the department that incurs them.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 10-MARK QUESTION
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Prepare departmental Trading and P&L Accounts.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: Create separate columns for each department; enter each department's sales, purchases and stock; charge direct expenses directly; apportion common expenses using specified ratios; calculate departmental gross and net profit; transfer departmental results to the General P&L Account where required; adjust for unrealised profit in closing stock from interdepartmental transfers. Check that total departmental figures reconcile with business totals.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: UNIT IV – DEPRECIATION
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 2-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 1. Define residual value.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: Residual value is the estimated amount recoverable on disposal of an asset at the end of its useful life, less disposal/removal costs.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 2. State the Straight Line Method formula.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: Annual depreciation=(Cost−Residual Value)/Useful Life.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 3. State the Written Down Value formula.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: Depreciation for a year=Opening WDV×Rate/100.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 5-MARK QUESTION
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Distinguish Straight Line and Written Down Value methods.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: SLM calculates a fixed annual amount using original cost less residual value over useful life. WDV applies a fixed rate to the opening reduced book value, so annual depreciation normally decreases. SLM uses original cost as the base; WDV uses current opening WDV. Use the method required by the question.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 10-MARK WORKED EXAMPLE
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: An asset costs Rs.25,000, has residual value Rs.5,000 and useful life 10 years. Find annual SLM depreciation and first three years of WDV depreciation at 10%.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: SLM=(25,000−5,000)/10=Rs.2,000 per year. WDV: Year 1=25,000×10%=2,500; closing=22,500. Year 2=22,500×10%=2,250; closing=20,250. Year 3=20,250×10%=2,025; closing=18,225. Show the year-wise asset value and depreciation working.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: UNIT V – SINGLE ENTRY SYSTEM
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 2-MARK QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 1. Define Single Entry System.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: It is an incomplete bookkeeping system in which both aspects of every transaction are not recorded systematically.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 2. What is a Statement of Affairs?
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: It is a statement listing assets and liabilities at a particular date; the difference is used to estimate capital/net worth.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 3. State the profit formula under Statement of Affairs method.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: Profit=Closing Capital+Drawings−Additional Capital−Opening Capital.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 5-MARK QUESTION
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Explain the features and defects of Single Entry System.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: It is incomplete and lacks uniform rules; personal accounts and cash records may be maintained while nominal and real accounts may be incomplete; a Trial Balance usually cannot be prepared; profit and financial position are less reliable; errors/fraud are difficult to detect; comparison and decision-making are impaired.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 10-MARK SOLVED EXAMPLE
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Opening capital Rs.1,20,000; closing assets Rs.2,10,000; closing outside liabilities Rs.60,000; drawings Rs.20,000; additional capital Rs.10,000. Find profit.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: Answer: Closing capital=2,10,000−60,000=1,50,000. Profit=1,50,000+20,000−10,000−1,20,000=Rs.40,000. State that the syllabus specifically prescribes numerical problems on Statement of Affairs method only.
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: MASTER MIXED REVISION – ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: A. SHORT DEFINITIONS TO MEMORISE
blocks.subject: Financial Accounting

blocks.text: 1. Algorithm – a finite, ordered set of steps for solving a problem. 2. Flowchart – a graphical representation of an algorithm using standard symbols. 3. Compiler – translates source code into target code and reports translation errors. 4. Recursion – a function or procedure solving a problem by calling itself on smaller cases. 5. Array – a collection of same-type elements accessed by index. 6. Pointer – a variable storing an address. 7. Data structure – an organisation of data for efficient storage and operations. 8. Stack – a LIFO structure. 9. Queue – a FIFO structure. 10. Binary tree – a tree in which each node has at most two children. 11. Microprocessor – a programmable processor integrated on a chip. 12. Interrupt – an event/request that diverts normal processor execution to a service routine. 13. Numerical error – the difference between a true value and a computed approximation. 14. Probability – a numerical measure of the likelihood of an event. 15. Correlation – a measure of association between variables. 16. Accounting – identification, measurement, recording, classification and communication of financial information. 17. Journal – chronological book of original entry. 18. Ledger – principal book containing separate accounts. 19. Trial Balance – statement of ledger balances. 20. Depreciation – systematic allocation/reduction of an asset's depreciable amount over useful life as taught in the textbook.

A REPEATABLE STUDY CYCLE
1. Preview the unit headings and identify what the unit teaches.
2. Read one concept at a time. Translate unfamiliar words into simple English.
3. Close the book and write the definition or method in your own words.
4. Work through one example while checking every step.
5. Solve another example without looking at the solution.
6. Mark the exact point where you made a mistake.
7. Return to the official textbook for its solved exercises and end-of-lesson questions.
8. Revisit the topic the next day, after three days and after one week.
